title: Add data residency defaults/validation + EU-only enterprise example
author: Bruno Silva
description:
Summary: This PR updates the redwood-terraform modules to support Hosted/Dedicated data residency settings with secure defaults and validation guardrails. It also adds an end-to-end example for an enterprise EU-only deployment (pinned to eu-west) and documents the expected behavior for multi-region configs when residency pinning is enabled.

Motivation: As part of Hosted data residency enforcement, we need to ensure enterprise accounts can set region pinning safely through IaC and avoid footguns that create RESIDENCY_REGION_MISMATCH errors at runtime (e.g., selecting an EU pinned region but configuring the provider/base_url pointing at a US endpoint). This module should (1) express residency settings explicitly, (2) validate inputs early, and (3) provide copy-pastable examples for Sales/SE and customer platform teams.

Changes:
- Adds variables for residency config: residency_enabled, pinned_region, allowed_regions, allow_cross_region_fallback (enterprise-only, default false).
- Adds validation rules to prevent invalid combinations:
  - pinned_region must be included in allowed_regions when both are set
  - allowed_regions must be non-empty when residency_enabled=true
  - allow_cross_region_fallback cannot be true unless residency_enabled=true
  - region strings validated against the supported region enum exposed by the module (eu-west, us-east, us-west, ap-southeast) (note: list matches current Hosted/Dedicated availability; doc calls out that regions expand over time).
- Adds opinionated defaults:
  - For enterprise preset: residency_enabled=true, allow_cross_region_fallback=false
  - For non-enterprise preset: residency_enabled defaults false (no behavior change)
- Adds example: examples/enterprise-eu-only-hosted-and-dedicated
  - EU-only org/project config
  - Notes for SDK/base URL configuration
  - Output snippets to help Support identify effective residency config quickly
- Updates README: documents how these settings map to platform behavior (gateway admission check + routing constraints).

Notes/Scope:
- This PR does not implement enforcement; it only wires module inputs -> control plane config and adds validation guardrails.
- Private/VPC deployments: module surfaces fields but README notes enforcement is handled inside the customer-managed environment and may differ; in our private module we will continue to treat pinned_region as an install-time parameter only.

Testing:
- terraform validate + fmt
- terratest: unit validation tests for invalid combos
- example plan runs in CI with mocked outputs

Rollout:
- Marking as safe for release; no breaking changes. Customers opting into residency pinning will need to ensure their endpoint/region selection matches (doc added).
commits: modules/control-plane: add residency variables + schema mapping
examples: add enterprise EU-only hosted + dedicated configuration
docs: update README with residency guidance and troubleshooting notes
tests: add terratest validation coverage for residency inputs
conversation:
Hanae Suzuki (review): Can we default allow_cross_region_fallback to false everywhere, not just enterprise preset? Even if the platform gate is enterprise-only, I’d rather be explicit and safe-by-default.
Bruno Silva (author): Agreed. Updated: variable default is false, preset just makes residency_enabled=true for enterprise. Added README note that cross-region fallback requires explicit allow_cross_region_fallback=true + feature flag on the platform side.

Marcus Lin (review): Validation: we should fail if pinned_region is set but residency_enabled=false. Otherwise you can accidentally set pinned_region and think you’re protected.
Bruno Silva (author): Added validation to require residency_enabled=true when pinned_region is non-null. Also updated example to set residency_enabled explicitly to reduce ambiguity.

Sean Gallagher (review): The example README should call out what Support should check when customers see a spike in denials (wrong base URL / wrong region). Also can we output the effective region policy to make debugging easier?
Bruno Silva (author): Added outputs residency_effective_allowed_regions and residency_effective_pinned_region, and added a Troubleshooting section to the example README with the usual misconfig cases.

Lauren Bishop (review): Dedicated module: do we want the same variables or should Dedicated just inherit from control-plane? Customers will want one knob.
Bruno Silva (author): Dedicated module now forwards to the same control-plane settings object. The example uses a single residency block at the org/project level; dedicated capacity references it. Added comment in dedicated README.

Chris Osei (review): Please link to ENG-2848 and call out that this is needed for beta onboarding. Also make sure the example name matches enablement materials (EU-only).
Bruno Silva (author): Updated PR description + example folder name/README title to match EU-only wording and added Linear links.
release_notes:
- Terraform modules now support configuring residency pinning (pinned_region/allowed_regions) with validation guardrails.
- Added enterprise EU-only example configuration for Hosted + Dedicated.
- New outputs expose effective residency settings to aid support/debugging.
